drug_class: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) combined with a Thiazide Diuretic
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two medicines in one pill to help lower your blood pressure more effectively than either medicine alone. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from serious problems.
how_it_works: Irbesartan works by blocking a chemical in your body called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten and narrow. By blocking it, your blood vessels relax and widen, making it easier for your heart to pump blood. Hydrochlorothiazide is a water pill that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and fluid from your body, which also lowers blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, especially when standing up quickly. Feeling tired or lightheaded. Needing to urinate more often (from the water pill). Headache. Low potassium levels, which can cause muscle cramps or weakness. Upset stomach or diarrhea.
warnings: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm your unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems. This medicine can lower your potassium or sodium levels, so your doctor may check your blood regularly. Avoid getting too dehydrated — drink enough fluids, especially in hot weather or when exercising. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, especially potassium supplements or other blood pressure drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is one tablet (150mg irbesartan / 12.5mg hydrochlorothiazide) taken once a day, with or without food. Your doctor may increase your dose to one tablet of the stronger strength (300mg / 12.5mg or 300mg / 25mg) once daily if needed. Always take it at the same time each day and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
